extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and project coordinators applying to ANR calls (AAPG and specific calls); panel members and expert reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evaluative standards that govern how the French National Research Agency (ANR) selects projects (Generic Call for Proposals AAPG and specific calls), including panel composition, peer review roles, confidentiality/ethics, two-stage evaluation, external reviews, rebuttal, ranking and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection of projects submitted to the Generic Call for Proposals (AAPG) and specific calls for proposals is based on the fundamental principle of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection relies on two types of independent reviewers belonging to the scientific communities (Scientific Evaluation Panels and Experts); decisions are founded on independent scientific peer review and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Evaluation Panels — composition and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Evaluation Panels consist of an office (a chairperson appointed by the Agency following a call for applications (one-year term renewable twice) and vice-chairs appointed by the ANR based on proposals from the chairperson) and French and international scientific figures from relevant research communities invited on the basis of proposals from the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gender parity and a balance of geography and affiliations are examined carefully when putting the panel together. Panel members individually assess a portfolio of projects based on strict criteria specific to the call, then debate the projects together and reach agreement on the list of projects they propose for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experts (external specialists) — role and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts, French or foreign specialists in the scientific field involved in the project, are invited to contribute by the ANR based on proposals from panel members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They assess projects independently based on criteria specific to the call without any discussion with the panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity, ethics, confidentiality, transparency and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Before accessing the project documents, panel members undertake to respect the principles of the ANR code of ethics and scientific integrity and the French National Charter for Research Integrity, protect the confidentiality of the information and declare that they have no conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If potential conflicts of interest arise (such as links with the project, previous collaborations, joint publications, professional or personal relationships), the members must inform the panel and leave the session when the project(s) concerned are discussed. The ANR undertakes to take appropriate actions if these rules are breached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 (AAPG) — pre-proposal evaluation and panel adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: In stage 1, the composition of the panel is adjusted to cover all the themes in the pre-proposals submitted. Each project is allocated to two panel members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An additional peer review may be requested if necessary, particularly for interdisciplinary projects. The committee meets to examine and discuss the projects before collectively deciding on a list of projects that will be invited to submit a full proposal in stage 2. An evaluation report summarising the panel's final opinion is sent to the coordinators of each eligible pre-proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 (AAPG) — full proposal evaluation, external reviews and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: In stage 2, the panel composition may be revised based on the scientific themes of the full proposals. Each project is allocated to two panel members, who suggest a list of potential external peer reviewers to obtain at least two external reviews for each proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The members assigned to evaluate the project review it individually based on the criteria in the AAPG text, taking into account the external reviews and any responses from the coordinator. The members then present an evaluation summary at a plenary meeting; after collective discussion, the panel ranks the best projects on a primary list and drafts a supplementary list of projects to be funded if co-funding is available or if budgets are reallocated. An evaluation report summarising the panel's final opinion is sent to the coordinators of each eligible proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: External peer review requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For stage 2 full proposals, panels must obtain at least two external reviews for each proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel members suggest potential external reviewers; external reviews are used alongside panel assessments when members evaluate the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal stage — coordinator responses to reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviews are sent to the scientific coordinators during the rebuttal stage so that they can pass on their comments if they find any inaccuracies in the reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator responses are taken into account by panel members when conducting their individual evaluations prior to the plenary discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of reviewers — two panel members per project
rubrics_metrics.description: Each project (both in stage 1 and stage 2) is allocated to two panel members for individual assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dual allocation is the basis for initial assessment, suggestion of external reviewers (stage 2), and presentation at plenary meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking and supplementary funding list
rubrics_metrics.description: After collective discussion, the panel ranks the best projects on a primary list and drafts a supplementary list of projects to be funded if co-funding is available or if budgets are reallocated due to project cancellations or postponements of other calls scheduled for the same budget year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplementary list is explicitly used to manage co-funding opportunities and budget reallocations; ranking decisions are collective outcomes of panel deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation reporting and communication to coordinators
rubrics_metrics.description: An evaluation report summarising the panel's final opinion is sent to the coordinators of each eligible pre-proposal and each eligible full proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports are provided after both stage 1 and stage 2 to communicate the panel's final opinion to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-selection appeals and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone involved in a project that has not been selected has two months from the date of notification of the decision or of the reasons for non-selection to send questions or appeals to contact.projetsnonselectionnes(at)anr.fr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requests are processed by the scientific departments and the chairpersons of the committees concerned in conjunction with the Legal Affairs Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition adjustments for thematic coverage and interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel composition is adjusted in stage 1 to cover all themes in pre-proposals and may be revised in stage 2 based on the scientific themes of full proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An additional peer review may be requested if necessary, particularly for interdisciplinary projects, ensuring appropriate expertise is involved in evaluation.
